headline: Jubo Dal leader confesses in Satkhira mob killing case
summary: Sadikul Islam Bhadu, general secretary of Parulia union Jubo Dal, admitted his involvement in the death of Wahiduzzaman Shamim.
details: Sadikul Islam Bhadu, general secretary of Parulia union Jubo Dal, has made a confessional statement in court regarding the mob killing of Wahiduzzaman Shamim in Satkhira’s Debhata.
The incident occurred after allegations that Shamim had "hurt religious sentiments" during a phone conversation recorded by a neighbor.
On October 12, Shamim’s house was attacked. He was subsequently admitted to the Sakhipur Upazila Health Complex for treatment.
The following evening, a mob broke down the hospital's back door and attacked Shamim in the presence of police, Ansar personnel, and doctors.
A murder case was filed on October 15, naming 10 people, including Sadikul Islam Bhadu and Fazlul Haq Amini, along with 250 unidentified individuals.
Sadikul surrendered to the court on October 28 and was denied bail. He was later placed on a three-day police remand for questioning.
Following the remand, Satkhira Magistrate Court-3 Judge Nusrat Jahan recorded his confessional statement under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
Another accused, Fazlul Haq Amini, has also previously provided a confession in court.
caption:
A Jubo Dal leader has confessed to his role in a mob killing in Satkhira.

Sadikul Islam Bhadu, general secretary of Parulia union Jubo Dal, has made a confessional statement in court regarding the mob killing of Wahiduzzaman Shamim in Satkhira’s Debhata.

The incident occurred after allegations that Shamim had "hurt religious sentiments" during a phone conversation recorded by a neighbor.

On October 12, Shamim’s house was attacked. He was subsequently admitted to the Sakhipur Upazila Health Complex for treatment.

The following evening, a mob broke down the hospital's back door and attacked Shamim in the presence of police, Ansar personnel, and doctors.

A murder case was filed on October 15, naming 10 people, including Sadikul Islam Bhadu and Fazlul Haq Amini, along with 250 unidentified individuals.

Sadikul surrendered to the court on October 28 and was denied bail. He was later placed on a three-day police remand for questioning.

Following the remand, Satkhira Magistrate Court-3 Judge Nusrat Jahan recorded his confessional statement under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

Another accused, Fazlul Haq Amini, has also previously provided a confession in court.

topic: EC retains old laws for UP polls
headline_marked: UP polls: [[EC sticks to old laws]], key reforms left out
headline: UP polls: EC sticks to old laws, key reforms left out
summary: Union Parishad elections will be held in five phases between January and May next year, bypassing recommendations from reform commissions.
details: The Election Commission (EC) has decided to hold the upcoming Union Parishad (UP) elections strictly under existing laws, ignoring recommendations from the Electoral and Local Government Reform Commissions.

The polls are scheduled to take place in five phases between January and May next year. Election Commissioner Abdur Rahmanel Masud stated that the EC will not go 'an inch beyond' the current legal framework.
Key proposed reforms that were left out include mandatory affidavits for UP candidates, rotational reservation of seats for women, and the introduction of indirect elections for mayors and chairmen.
Other recommendations included requiring MPO-enlisted teachers to resign before contesting and amending the Constitution to allow the EC to schedule local elections independently.
Reform commission members argued that these changes could have reduced the election process duration from 225 days to just one or two months and significantly cut costs.
Between 2021 and 2024, the government spent approximately Tk 2,300 crore on local government elections.
While the government has abolished party symbols in local elections, experts and former commission members warn that structural reforms remain largely unaddressed.
Adviser Zahed Ur Rahman noted that proposals requiring legislative changes must first be approved by parliament, and implementation will depend on political consensus.

Other recommendations included requiring MPO-enlisted teachers to resign before contesting and amending the Constitution to allow the EC to schedule local elections independently.

Reform commission members argued that these changes could have reduced the election process duration from 225 days to just one or two months and significantly cut costs.

Between 2021 and 2024, the government spent approximately Tk 2,300 crore on local government elections.
